definition: Able to recover or adapt after difficulty or strain.
example: The resilient team learned from the failed launch and tried a revised approach.
nuance: Resilience means recovering or adapting; it does not require being untouched by harm.
prompt: A community rebuilds and adapts after a damaging setback.
options: The resilient community rebuilt its services after the storm.
The resilient community never encountered any challenge, so its capacity to recover was demonstrated.
The resilient plan resisted every change even when conditions demanded adaptation.
The resilient community gave up after the storm and abandoned the town for good.
reasons: This sentence demonstrates the meaning: able to recover or adapt after difficulty or strain.
Without a challenge, this sentence does not demonstrate recovery capacity.
Rigid resistance to necessary adaptation is not resilience.
Giving up and leaving after damage reverses the meaning; resilience means bouncing back, not collapsing.

practice.prompt: A student gets a low grade on her first chemistry exam of the year.
options: The resilient student was so discouraged by one low grade that she dropped chemistry for the rest of the year.
The resilient student was too shy to raise her hand and ask the teacher about the exam.
The resilient student hid the exam in a drawer and pretended the test had never happened.
The resilient student reviewed her mistakes, joined a study group, and earned a B on the next test.
reasons: Quitting after a single setback is the opposite of recovering from it.
Shyness about speaking up is reticence, a look-alike idea that has nothing to do with recovery.
Denying a setback is avoidance; a resilient person faces the difficulty and adapts.
She bounced back from the setback by changing how she prepared, which is exactly what resilience looks like.
